scenes.title: Make the design executable
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous experiment design.
scenes.narration: Your design describes the claim and check. A validation test plan organises how you will carry it out responsibly: steps, owners, permissions, records and review. Completing this lesson creates a plan. It does not run a test, grant access or prove demand.

scenes.title: Keep one claim and protocol
scenes.narration: Carry forward the specific group, claim and decision from Lesson 24. Write preparation, check and close steps with consistent instructions. Keep the method aligned with the claim. If the scope changes, document why and update the design instead of silently changing the question.

scenes.title: Check access and readiness
scenes.visual: Editable pending and confirmed permission cards.
scenes.narration: Name relevant participants or sources, permission status and how people can decline or stop. A named contact is not confirmed help. Assign owners, timing and effort limits. Keep critical constraints visible; missing permission may mean readiness is pending even when all fields are complete.

scenes.title: Record without inventing
scenes.visual: Editable source code, signal and deviation columns.
scenes.narration: Plan anonymous evidence records with date, context and observable signals. Keep interpretation separate. Record deviations from the protocol and limitations rather than hiding them. Do not prefill expected findings as results or collect personal information you do not need.

scenes.title: Plan stop and review paths
scenes.visual: Editable supportive, weakening, inconclusive and stop cards.
scenes.narration: Preserve the criteria from the design. Decide how supportive, weakening or inconclusive information affects the next step. Record a review date and decision owner. Set stop conditions and a fallback for access, privacy or resource problems. No result should automatically approve a venture.

scenes.title: Close the design module
scenes.visual: Actual approved Lesson 25 worksheet recording and five-deliverable list.
scenes.narration: Create your Validation Test Plan and review your starting brief, assumption register, priority plan and experiment design. All five lessons close Module 2.1 when locally self-completed. Research execution remains separate. The next module prepares neutral customer conversations, with permission and evidence limits intact.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Organise the work before executing the check.

children: A
test plan
coordinates the experiment design, protocol, owners, access, evidence records and review. A
protocol
is the consistent sequence and instructions. A
deviation
is a change from that plan that must be recorded.
Confirm one priority claim and relevant group/context.
Write preparation, check and close steps.
Record pending/confirmed permissions and voluntary participation.
Assign owner, timing, effort and dependencies.
Plan anonymous evidence records and deviations.
Preserve interpretation criteria, stop/fallback and review decisions.
Illustrative plan:

a directions-clarity task remains pending until access and voluntary participation are arranged. A document review can be a permitted fallback, but answers a different question and must be labeled accordingly.

Lesson completion is not operational readiness. Pending permission can remain honestly pending with a fallback; no recruitment, recording, payment collection or test execution occurs here. Do not fill planned records with expected results. If the method or claim changes, document the reason and revise the design.
Review Module 2.1 deliverables
Review validation starting brief
Review assumption register
Review priority plan
Review experiment design
These drafts remain separate; nothing is merged or verified automatically.
